parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct, no trans-specific traveller-facing restrictions (no facility bans, no document screening friction, no custody-placement rules, no care denial), and legal gender recognition exist. The documented negatives are societal: Pride-scoped violence (assault, flag burnings, eggs), bias incidents with unclear national coverage, weakly enforced anti-discrimination law, uneven official response, and victim support routed mainly through civil society. This is tier-3 societal hostility with thin-but-existing recourse in a functioning rule-of-law state — not state targeting, not universal-exposure measures. A visitor's exposure is low: friction, occasional hostility, imperfect police follow-through.

entry_documents.protection: Legal gender recognition exists domestically as a climate signal; no documented border friction or marker-checking practices against visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented interaction between document presentation and border/investigation systems for visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: No reports of official-condoned violence (2023 foreign HR report); functioning courts implied by rule-of-law character.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in public services since 2016, though rarely enforced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Generic victim-support services present heteronomative hurdles; recourse runs through civil society instead.

care_services.protection: Legal gender recognition without medical-treatment requirement confirmed by health ministry in 2024; civil-registry amendment status unresolved.
care_services.interaction: Resident-facing recognition machinery; not a direct visitor protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented societal hostility: 2023 Pride assault with minor injuries, flag burnings, eggs thrown; political-party youth wing anti-LGBTIQ sentiment; 'prevalent and under-reported' NGO violence characterisation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Head of state, ombudsman, legislative head and government head condemned attacks; police investigated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Interior minister silent; enforcement of protections 'very rarely enforced' — police follow-through on bias incidents weak.

minors_guardians.protection: Education anti-discrimination rules in force since 2003 (weakly enforced, sexuality-focused).

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Pride-scoped assaults and harassment in 2023; under-recorded outside Pride period; 25 direct bias incidents documented by one trans organisation, counts without denominators.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police received reports and investigated; senior officials condemned; civil society provides counselling, advocacy, safe spaces.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Authorities record incidents without tracking case numbers — no reliable enforcement trend; recourse quality uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Anti-discrimination enforcement vague and very rarely enforced; institutional shortcomings in hate-crime framework documented (Jan 2025 report).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-society victim support operational; equality-body advocacy achieved recognition-procedure reform in 2022.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Marriage/partnership regime unresolved in sources; registry sub-article amendment unresolved — open questions, light weight.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: documented public hostility with some violence, functioning but imperfect police response, condemnations from leadership. Here hostility is narrower (Pride-scoped) and no trans-specific enforcement failures documented, but protections are also weaker (rarely enforced law), placing it around the same level.

Below that anchor: it has working oversight boards, prompt remedies and broad social tolerance; here enforcement is 'very rarely enforced', official response was uneven and slow, and NGOs describe prevalent under-reported violence. The gap is roughly one step.

Above that anchor: 0.55-E shows systematic-ish service ejection and stalled investigations; here the documented hostility is event-scoped, no traveller-facing service denial or facility restrictions appear, and institutional climate is explicitly among the region's most progressive.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime presents no traveller-facing legal exposure: no criminal statute applied to gender presentation, no facility or custody rules aimed at trans people, no documented border or document friction. The operative negatives are societal hostility — concentrated at the capital Pride event (assaults, flag burnings) with an under-recorded baseline — plus weak enforcement of written protections and hate-crime machinery with institutional shortcomings, meaning recourse after an incident is uncertain and largely civil-society-mediated. State actors are neither perpetrators nor organised tolerators of targeting; leadership condemned the violence, though inconsistently. This is tier-3 hostility with thin recourse in a functioning state: materially safer than 0.55-tier friction regimes, below the 0.85 tier where remedies demonstrably operate.
